``` {r import dataset, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

dat_1 <- read_csv("dat_1_m.csv")

```

``` {r compliance worried sch}

### Database

# 1. Calculate person-level statistics (worry mean and compliance rates)
dat_compliance_and_worry <- dat_1 %>%
  group_by(id_esm) %>%
  summarise(
    worried_mean = mean(as.numeric(gsub(",", ".", as.character(worried))), na.rm = TRUE),
    compl_n = sum(!is.na(worried)),
    maxday = max(day[!is.na(worried)], na.rm = TRUE),
    # Compliance rate until the last active day (active compliance)
    all_answer_active = maxday * 8,
    compl_pct_active = (compl_n / all_answer_active) * 100,
    # Absolute compliance rate calculated for the total 28 days
    all_answer_absolute = 28 * 8,
    compl_pct_absolute = (compl_n / all_answer_absolute) * 100
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# 2. Extract fix baseline MSS-B scores per person
dat_mssb_scores <- dat_1 %>%
  distinct(id_esm, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  select(id_esm, sch_neg, sch_pos, sch_dis)

# 3. Merge datasets to create the clean person-level dataframe
dat_person_level <- dat_mssb_scores %>%
  left_join(dat_compliance_and_worry, by = "id_esm") %>%
  select(id_esm, sch_neg, sch_pos, sch_dis, worried_mean, compl_pct_active, compl_pct_absolute)

# View the final person-level dataset
tibble(dat_person_level)

### Correlation

# Select numeric columns for the correlation matrix
cor_data <- dat_person_level %>%
  select(sch_neg, sch_pos, sch_dis, worried_mean, compl_pct_active, compl_pct_absolute)

# Run correlation analysis (Pearson by default)
cor_matrix <- rcorr(as.matrix(cor_data), type = "pearson")

# Print the correlation coefficients (r)
print("Correlation coefficients (r):")
print(round(cor_matrix$r, digits = 2))

# Print the significance levels (p)
print("Significance levels (p):")
print(round(cor_matrix$P, digits = 3))

```

``` {r compl worried sch lmer}

# 1. Left join compl_pct_active
dat_1 <- dat_1 %>%
  left_join(
    dat_person_level %>% select(id_esm, compl_pct_active), 
    by = "id_esm")

# 2. Run separate models for each schizotypy dimension as a safety check

m_dc <- lmer(worried ~ sch_dis * compl_pct_active + (1 | id_esm), data = dat_1)
cat("\n--- SCH_DIS ---\n")
summary(m_dc)

m_pc <- lmer(worried ~ sch_pos * compl_pct_active + (1 | id_esm), data = dat_1)
cat("\n--- SCH_POS ---\n")
summary(m_pc)

m_nc <- lmer(worried ~ sch_neg * compl_pct_active + (1 | id_esm), data = dat_1)
cat("\n--- SCH_NEG ---\n")
summary(m_nc)

# 3. Run the large, combined model to test unique predictive effects
m_dpnc <- lmer(worried ~ (sch_dis + sch_pos + sch_neg) * compl_pct_active + (1 | id_esm), data = dat_1)
cat("\n--- SCH_ALL ---\n")
summary(m_dpnc)

```

``` {r compl worried sch lmer visu}

library(interactions)
library(jtools)
library(ggplot2)

### DEZORGANIZED
colors_dis <- c("#E2C2E3", "#BC80BD", "#804881")

plot_dis_int <- interact_plot(
  model = m_dpnc,
  pred = sch_dis,
  modx = compl_pct_active,
  modx.values = c(18.52, 30.48, 38.39), 
  plot.points = FALSE,                  
  interval = TRUE,                      
  x.label = "Dezorganizált dimenzió",
  y.label = "Az aggodalom prediktált szintje",
  main.title = "A dezorganizált skizotípia és az aktív együttműködés interakciós hatása az aggodalomra",
  legend.main = "Az együttműködés mértéke")

plot_dis_int <- plot_dis_int + 
  scale_color_gradientn(
    colors = colors_dis, 
    breaks = c(18.52, 30.48, 38.39),
    labels = c("Átlag - 1 SD", "Átlag", "Átlag + 1 SD"),
    guide = guide_legend()) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colors = colors_dis, 
    breaks = c(18.52, 30.48, 38.39),
    labels = c("Átlag - 1 SD", "Átlag", "Átlag + 1 SD"),
    guide = guide_legend())

print(plot_dis_int)
```
